acceptance_criteria.criterion: renderChunksToText is exported from chunk-renderer.ts and callable with a JSONL string argument
For single-namespace JSONL input, the returned string contains only assembled prose text from AI turns with no section headers, no tool call JSON, and no tool results
For dual-namespace JSONL input (both ns.length === 0 and ns.length > 0 entries), the returned string contains ## Outer Agent and ## Inner Agent section headers with prose beneath each
When the input JSONL is empty or contains no AI text content, the function returns '*No dialogue recorded.*\n'
The function is pure (no I/O, no side effects) — consistent with the existing renderers in the same module
The return value is terminated with '\n'

summary: Added renderChunksToText() public renderer and extractTextFromMessages() private helper to chunk-renderer.ts. The new renderer extracts prose-only text from AI turns (no tool-call JSON, no tool results) and returns it as a Markdown string. Single-namespace files render as flat prose; dual-namespace files get ## Outer Agent / ## Inner Agent section headers. Returns '*No dialogue recorded.\n' for empty or content-free input. Updated module doc comment to list renderChunksToText alongside the existing three renderers. TypeScript build passes cleanly (npm run build); all 111 existing chunk-renderer tests pass.

comments.note: Fixed EC index comment block in mcp-server/tests/gui/chunk-renderer-text.test.ts. Also tightened EC-4, EC-5, EC-6 descriptions to match the actual test scenarios. Pure comment change — no test logic or assertions altered.

Line 1191: `[...nsMap.keys()].some(k => k !== '')` allocates a temporary array to detect sub-agent namespaces. `nsMap.size > 1` is a semantically equivalent O(1) alternative (single-namespace files always have exactly one key: ''; dual-namespace files have 2+). The current form is slightly more explicit about the intent ('any key that is not the outer namespace') and perfectly fine at the scale of namespace counts — noting as a style observation only, not a blocking concern.

[documentation-forward] renderChunksToText() JSDoc (lines 1160-1178) describes 'Dual-namespace files' but the current implementation supports N inner namespaces (all labeled '## Inner Agent'). The doc comment should clarify that multiple inner namespaces each get a '## Inner Agent' section header and that label distinguishability is not guaranteed for N > 1 inners. Add a note so future contributors understand the current design constraint before adding N-inner support.
